note: The cross-ecosystem reproducibility corpus of the canonical SBOM projection.
Every entry names a synthetic, immutable lockfile, the subject purl an auditor
supplies for it, and the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes that lockfile projects to.
The hash is a FROZEN pin: it changes only when the projection changes, and the
projection changing is exactly what the pin exists to make observable.
The same constants are re-derived on every platform that runs the suite -- the
development machine (Windows) and continuous integration (Linux) -- so a one-byte
divergence between two operating systems turns one of the two runs red against
the same file. Recomputing a pin to make a run green is the one edit forbidden
here: it converts a measurement into a transcription.
Real lockfiles are deliberately ABSENT from this file. They change legitimately
with every dependency bump, so they carry invariants instead of pins.
